cohort: 608 women who delivered their first child between 1990-1997
finding: Forceps delivery was associated with a significantly higher risk of pelvic organ prolapse, levator avulsion, and larger hiatal area compared to vacuum and normal vaginal deliveries, while cesarean delivery was associated with a lower risk.
mod_finding: Compared to normal vaginal delivery, forceps delivery was associated with higher odds of POP and levator avulsion, while there were no significant differences observed with vacuum delivery.
